baseCurrency.name: Florentine Florin / Venetian Ducat
baseCurrency.description: Standard gold coin of ~3.5 grams pure gold (24 karat), the premier international trade currency of late medieval Europe, the Mediterranean, and the Levant.

currencies.name: Ottoman Akçe
currencies.description: Silver coin minted under Murad II and Mehmed II; ~40-45 akce equaled 1 gold ducat/florin in 1450.

currencies.name: Silver Liang (Tael)
currencies.description: Traditional Chinese unit of weight in silver (~37g silver = ~3.5 gold florins). Circulated alongside strings of copper cash (wen) and Baocao paper notes.

currencies.name: Pound Sterling
currencies.description: 240 Tower pence of sterling silver (0.925 fine). 1 pound sterling was worth ~3.3 gold florins. Gold nobles circulated at 6s 8d (1/3 pound).

currencies.name: Livre tournois
currencies.description: French money of account; ~3.5 livres tournois to 1 gold florin / ecu d or.

currencies.name: Rhenish Gulden
currencies.description: The standard gold coin of the Holy Roman Empire established by the Rhenish Coinage Union.

currencies.name: Maravedí / Dobla
currencies.description: Standard money of account in Castile. 1 gold dobla de la banda was worth 365-375 maravedis (~1 florin).

currencies.name: Portuguese Cruzado / Real
currencies.description: Portuguese gold cruzado minted under Alfonso V, equal in gold content to the Venetian ducat.

currencies.name: Mamluk Ashrafi (Dinar)
currencies.description: Introduced by Mamluk Sultan al-Ashraf Barsbay in 1425 to match the weight and purity of the Venetian ducat.

currencies.name: Vijayanagara Varaha (Pagoda)
currencies.description: Gold varaha (also called pagoda by Europeans) featuring Hindu deities, standard trade currency of South India and Indian Ocean spice routes.

currencies.name: Timurid Kepeki Dinar / Toman
currencies.description: Timurid currency system centered on the silver dinar and super-unit toman (10,000 dinars).

currencies.name: Russian Denga / Ruble
currencies.description: Silver denga coins minted in Moscow, Novgorod, and Tver; 200 denga made up the ruble of account (~1 florin).

currencies.name: Lübeck / Nordic Mark
currencies.description: Silver mark of the Hanseatic League and the Wendish Coinage Union; standard unit across Denmark, Sweden, and the Baltic littoral.

currencies.name: Japanese Mon / Ryō
currencies.description: Imported copper cash (Torasen) and gold banryō circulating across Muromachi Japan under the Ashikaga shogunate.

currencies.name: Gold Mithqal / Cowrie Standard
currencies.description: Trans-Saharan gold dinar/mithqal standard combined with cowrie shell trade strings across West Africa and the Swahili coast.

currencies.name: Quachtli & Cacao Standard
currencies.description: Mesoamerican monetary standard based on standardized woven cotton cloaks (quachtli) and cacao beans used for tribute and trade.

currencies.name: Mit'a Reciprocity & Cumbi
currencies.description: Incan economic unit based on standardized fine cumbi cloth weaves, state storehouse tallies, and communal mit'a labor obligations.
